paper_metadata.title: Structure and mechanical properties of refractory complex concentrated alloys with late 3d transition metal and Ti/Al additions
paper_metadata.journal: International Journal of Refractory Metals and Hard Materials

evidence.quote: Advanced high-temperature materials, including refractory complex concentrated alloys (RCCAs), require precipitation strengthening to achieve a balance between high-temperature strength and room-temperature damage tolerance.
This study explored an alloy design strategy involving additions of late 3d transition metals (Co, Fe, Ni) combined with Ti or Al to a single-phase body-centred cubic (bcc) Nb85Mo5Ta5V5 (at.%) RCCA.

machine_learning_models.name: Support Vector Regression
machine_learning_models.dataset: RCCAs yield strength values at 22 °C and 1000 °C
machine_learning_models.validation: bagging with 1000 randomly selected subsets, each comprising 70% of the initial dataset

evidence.quote: The yield strengths of the alloys at 22 and 1000 °C were predicted using a data-driven machine learning model [50]. The model employed the Support Vector Regression (SVR) algorithm with a radial basis function kernel [51]. A set of nine features – valence electron concentration (VEC), enthalpy of mixing (ΔH_mix), electronegativity difference (Δχ), configurational entropy (ΔS_mix), work function (φ), shear modulus (G), and the γ, Λ, and Ω parameters – was used to train the model [52–54]. The training dataset included yield strength values for RCCAs at both room (22 °C) and elevated (1000 °C) temperatures.
